purpose: Diazoxide is used to treat low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) caused by the pancreas making too much insulin, especially in certain tumors or conditions. It helps keep your blood sugar from dropping too low. In some cases, it has also been used to quickly lower dangerously high blood pressure.
how_it_works: Your pancreas releases a hormone called insulin that lowers your blood sugar. Diazoxide works by blocking the pancreas from releasing too much insulin, which helps keep your blood sugar at a safe level. Think of it like putting a gentle brake on your pancreas so it does not overwork and cause your sugar to drop too low.
common_side_effects: Fluid retention or swelling (especially in your legs or face), increased heart rate, nausea, stomach upset, loss of appetite, excessive hair growth (especially in children), and changes in blood sugar levels. You may also notice your urine output increases.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have heart disease, kidney problems, or are pregnant, as diazoxide can cause serious fluid buildup around the heart or in the lungs. It can also cause high blood sugar if the dose is too high. Regular blood sugar monitoring is very important. Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: For low blood sugar in adults, the usual dose is 3 to 8 milligrams per kilogram of body weight per day, divided into 2 or 3 doses taken by mouth. Children may be dosed differently based on their weight. Your doctor will find the right dose for you and may adjust it over time based on how your blood sugar responds.
